newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-RANDGOLD RESOURCES LISTS FOR GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-RANDGOLD RESOURCES LISTS FOR GROWTH.

text.p: African gold exploration company Randgold Resources Ltd said on Thursday it planned to raise $126-161 million by listing seven million shares on the London Stock Exchange to help fund existing and new projects.
South African parent company Randgold and Exploration Ltd said its international subsidiary, Randgold Resources, would start trading on the LSE on June 30 at a price between $18 and $23 a share.

"Randgold Resources...has reached the stage where its strategic development requires a substantial capital injection. The directors believe the most effective way of facilitating this is to combine the raising of capital with a listing on the London Stock Exchange," the company said.
Randgold said it could not directly finance Randgold Resources due to existing foreign exchange controls.

"An international offer of approximately seven million new shares and global depositary securities is being led by HSBC Investment Bank. The target date for unconditional dealings in RRL shares and GDSs to start on the LSE is 30 June 1997."
Pricing of the offer is scheduled for the preceding week.
Randgold said the listing would raise funding for the further development of its Syama gold mine and its Loulo gold project in Mali.
It said it would have around $253 million available for capital expenditure, including existing project finance. Of this $68 million would be used to develop Syama and $39 million allocated to Loulo.
Golden Ridge in Tanzania would receive $38 million.
Exploration, including Morila in Mali, Nielle in Ivory Coast and Sanmatenga in Burkina Faso, would receive $70 million.

An increased capital base would also support the acquisition of existing underperforming gold mines and projects in Sub-Saharan Africa and allow for exploration with the aim of discovering bulk tonnage shallow deposits, the company said.

Randgold Resources said its growth strategy in the short-term was to establish Syama as a world class mine, develop Loulo and Golden Ridge and make a mining decision on at least one other project in the next 24 months.
Longer-term, it planned to bring a new property into production every 18 months to two years.

"Our mission is to build a world class, gold-focused, African resource company by the discovery, evaluation and acquisition of minng opportunities," Randgold Resources managing director Mark Bristow told a pre-listing presentation.

Following the listing, Randgold would hold 50 percent of Randgold Resources, the International Finance Corp (IFC) five percent and other shareholders, mainly large international institutions, the remaining 45 perent, the company said.

The IFC's stake arises out of its role in giving a $35 million loan to Randgold Resources for a planned a $68 million three-year project programme, announced earlier this week, to increase production to 270,000 ounces a year.
Syama's March quarter production was 35,312 ounces and Randgold said it expected the mine to produce 40,500 ounces in the current June quarter.

A recently-completed due diligence report quantified Randgold Resources attributable proven and probable reserves as 3.36 million ounces of gold at 3.83 grams/tonne. The company said its total gold resources were 7.34 million ounces.

Randgold Resources also announced on Thursday that it planned to acquire a further 31 percent of the Loulo gold project, which would raise its stake to 51 percent. It will recommend mining Loulo within the next month.
